situation:
You are the human resources coordinator for the CEDAR HOLLOW MUNICIPAL UTILITIES DEPARTMENT, the city department that provides water and sewer service to about forty thousand residents and pays its own way out of rates. The city manager (judge) has asked to meet with you about a conflict between two senior employees.

The founding director, who built the department from a two-person office and has kept the peace between the two of them for years, retires at the end of the quarter. The field operations superintendent and the billing services supervisor disagree over who directs crews on emergency repairs. The disagreement has been running for months and the retirement has sharpened it.

Crews now take verbal directions from both and follow whichever came last. The emails the two exchange have grown pointed and are copied to staff who have no part in the matter, and two of those emails have already been requested under the state's open records law. Residents calling about repair delays hear one account from field operations and another from billing.

Handling it inside the department, with a documented conversation with each employee and a memo restating who directs crews, costs nothing but leaves a thin record if either files a formal complaint once the director is gone. A formal investigation with an outside mediator would build that record, but it draws on a budget the council froze when it froze rates, and it becomes a public document both employees will read.

The city manager (judge) wants you to analyze what is driving the conflict, recommend how the department should resolve and document it, and explain what should be put in writing, to whom, and through which channel. The city manager (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the city manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the city manager (judge) for the city that operates the CEDAR HOLLOW MUNICIPAL UTILITIES DEPARTMENT. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the human resources coordinator to recommend whether the conflict between the field operations superintendent and the billing services supervisor should be handled inside the department or through a formal investigation with an outside mediator, to say what each course costs, and to describe what should be written down, who should receive it, and how.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up paying for this, the crews or the residents?
If the council asks why we chose this, what do we tell them?
